 eThekwini steps up inner city preparations ahead of festive season 
 Saturday, November 21, 2026 
 The eThekwini Municipality has stepped up preparations for the festive season, with City Manager Musa Mbhele leading a walkabout through the Durban inner city to assess service delivery, infrastructure conditions and progress on urban regeneration.
 The walkabout, conducted earlier this week, aimed to identify problem areas, assess ongoing inner-city improvement initiatives and check how infrastructure has withstood the heavy rains experienced since September.
 Durban traditionally experiences an influx of visitors during the festive season, placing increased demand on municipal services, including water, electricity, sanitation, waste management, traffic control and public safety.
 The period is also important for the city's economy, supporting tourism, hospitality, small businesses, informal traders and residents, who depend on seasonal economic activity.
 Mbhele said preparations must be visible on the ground - well ahead of the festive season peak.
 “Durban is a city people choose to come home to and celebrate in. Our focus is on making sure services are ready to meet the higher demand this festive season brings. That work must happen now, with officials on the ground checking progress and fixing what needs to be fixed before the peak arrives,” Mbhele said.
 During the walkabout, the delegation inspected stormwater drains, roads, pavements and street lighting to identify areas that need attention for prioritisation as the rainy season continues.
 Mbhele emphasised that a well-managed inner city is central to economic growth, investment and job creation, adding that the benefits of urban regeneration must extend to residents throughout the year, not only during peak seasons.
 “An inner city that is clean, safe and well run is an economic asset. When the basics work, businesses stay, new investment follows and opportunities open up for our residents. Regeneration is not about appearance. It is about growing the economy of this city,” he said.
 He also called for stronger oversight by municipal managers, emphasising the need for hands-on leadership and accountability in monitoring service delivery.
 “Raising the standard of service delivery will not happen from behind a desk. Every manager must know the state of the areas and projects they are responsible for. Reports must be backed by what is seen on the ground. Managers must go out, check the quality of the work and make sure it is sustained,” Mbhele said.
 While acknowledging progress in the inner city, Mbhele said more needs to be done to meet residents' expectations.
 “There is work happening in the inner city and it is visible. But residents expect more, and they deserve more. We will not be satisfied until the inner city is clean, safe and working for everyone who lives, works and does business here,” he said.
 The walkabout came as Durban strengthens its international profile following its selection as South Africa's preferred host city in the country's bid to host the 2036 or 2040 Olympic and Paralympic Games.
 The South African Sports Confederation and Olympic Committee (SASCOC) announced the selection on 29 October 2026.
 Mbhele said the development places greater responsibility on the municipality to improve its standards and ensure the city remains well managed.
 Issues identified during the walkabout will be referred to the relevant municipal teams for intervention, with follow-up inspections planned to monitor progress. – SAnews.gov.za
